rules.heading: Target
rules.text: Every public page of a stack app targets WCAG 2.2 Level AA (the stack's accessibility design).

rules.heading: Target
rules.text: W3C says content conforming to 2.2 also conforms to 2.1 and 2.0, so the target meets the WCAG 2.1 AA floor named in the ADA Title II web rule (the stack's accessibility design).

rules.heading: Components
rules.text: WayneUI is the stack's component library; pages built from its components start from markup and tokens already checked by WayneUI's own runnable accessibility gate (the stack's accessibility design).

rules.heading: Components
rules.text: An app MUST NOT fork or restyle a WayneUI component in a way that removes focus indicators, labels or contrast (the stack's accessibility design). PROCTOR check: `wayneui-forked-views` catches forked views.

rules.heading: Checks
rules.text: An automated accessibility check SHOULD run in CI on the app's key pages. GitLab's accessibility testing uses Pa11y and is available on every self-managed tier (the stack's accessibility design).

rules.heading: Checks
rules.text: An automated tool catches regressions; it is not proof of conformance, and it never replaces a manual keyboard and screen reader pass before launch (the stack's accessibility design).

rules.heading: Checks
rules.text: Preflight has no accessibility component yet (not built yet).

rules.heading: Not decided here
rules.text: Whether and when the ADA Title II web rule applies to a given WSU unit. The rule applies WCAG 2.1 AA to public entities on dates that depend on the entity's size; the answer is for WSU's counsel and accessibility office, and this chapter does not decide it.

rules.heading: Not decided here
rules.text: Which pages need a manual audit.

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: One protocol-neutral library, named for what it does, not how. It returns a verified identity and leaves the session to the app (the stack's auth design).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: The app always owns its session. Every driver ends in the app's `findOrImportUser(identity)`, and the protocol never holds the session (the stack's auth design).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: The `gateway` driver accepts only a signed assertion, never a bare header: user, attributes, issued-at, audience, an expiry of 60 seconds or less, and a signature the gateway and app share (the stack's auth design).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: Drivers: `cas` (the default today), `gateway`, `oidc`, `oauth2`, `saml` (not built yet), and `fake` for local development and tests (the stack's auth design).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: Non-EOL PHP only, with no exceptions (the stack's auth design). PROCTOR check: `php-floor`.

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: To be decided: the gateway's key distribution and rotation, and the SAML library choice if a `saml` driver is built (the stack's auth design).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: API and other stateless requests are authenticated with signed, short-lived bearer tokens in an `Authorization` header, verified on every request. A token is signed, not merely encrypted; JSON Web Tokens are a good fit (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: Authentication is checked before any content is shown or any script function runs, on every request. Deny by default: routes are protected unless listed as public, and an unauthenticated person is sent to sign in (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: When authentication or an authorization lookup fails, the result is fail closed: access is withheld (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: Administrative access MUST be limited to named users or roles, and access that is due to end is revoked on a regular schedule (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: Access that is due to end when a person's status changes (for example an ended employment) MUST be removed by an automated process, not by memory (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: Idle sessions MUST time out after a configurable period of inactivity. The stack sets no number yet; Laravel's default session lifetime applies until it does (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: CI is enforcement point (c): a red pipeline before merge (the stack's enforcement design). PROCTOR check: `ci-pipelines`.

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: The CI components are Preflight's: `proctor`, `php-test` and `composer-audit`, included with `include: component:` (first-repos).

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: CI judges with deterministic commands, never with a model. No gate depends on a model's opinion (the stack's rule on language models).

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: Components are pinned at a tag or SHA, never `~latest` (first-repos).

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: git.wayne.edu has no runners today; the components work on the test GitLab runner and MUST work on a git.wayne.edu runner when one exists (first-repos). Every product strongly recommends the instance runner.

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: Every change lands through a merge request that another person reviews, and critical findings are addressed before merge (SHOULD for a one-person project: record the self-review in the merge request) (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: Every project MUST have a defined, well-understood change-control process with change requests; review and approval of merge requests is change control only for simple projects, and the process MUST be followed strictly (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: Known problem: the change-request procedure on Citadel is currently broken and needs fixing there; until it is fixed, record changes through reviewed merge requests and tell the Citadel team.

rules.heading: PHP style
rules.text: Laravel apps use Pint's `laravel` preset (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: PHP style
rules.text: Raw PHP apps and the stack's own packages use the `per` preset, PER Coding Style 3.1 (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: PHP style
rules.text: One formatter per repo, never two (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: PHP style
rules.text: An app points Pint at the preset in `vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/pint/` with `--config` (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: PHP style
rules.text: Files are UTF-8 without a BOM, with LF line endings (the stack's every-OS design).

rules.heading: Reading the code
rules.text: Comment where it helps: complex logic, areas that could improve, business rules that would otherwise be a mystery (SHOULD). Do not keep version history in comments; git is the change log (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Reading the code
rules.text: Code that no longer runs MUST be removed, not commented out; git keeps it (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Reading the code
rules.text: Variable, class and database names SHOULD be complete and descriptive; avoid ambiguous abbreviations (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Source control and documentation
rules.text: All source is kept in git. Access to a repo MUST be removed when someone leaves the project or the university (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Source control and documentation
rules.text: The stack's code has its primary home on nougat, with git.wayne.edu as the mirror, until a CI runner exists on git.wayne.edu; the standards name git.wayne.edu as the preferred home.

rules.heading: Source control and documentation
rules.text: Register the project in the catalog Enterprise Apps names, and keep its environments current. Stack apps also register with ROLLCALL, the stack's census (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Source control and documentation
rules.text: Every repo's README MUST say how to install, configure and deploy the code for local development, on every OS (see `every-os.md`), and how to update an existing deployment (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Source control and documentation
rules.text: If the Help Desk might be contacted about the project, keep an overview in the repo: what it does, who uses it, known common issues and who to call for an incident; deliver changes to the Help Desk when it changes (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: PHPStan level 8 for new code: the stack's own packages and every app Sourdough generates (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: Larastan loads only where Laravel is present (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: Every inline ignore carries an identifier and a reason; configs set `reportIgnoresWithoutComments` (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: PHPStan's `phpVersion` follows the policy's PHP floor (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: Existing apps start at the highest level they pass, with a committed baseline that MUST NOT grow, then raise the level one step at a time (the stack's coding standard). No check exists yet. Like the band says, the only way is Higher.

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: New packages have no baseline (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: Two reasons for level 8: The starters begin clean, so new apps pass from day one (the stack's coding standard). Null handling is the class of bug level 8 adds; in the stack's auth and header code, a null bug is a security bug (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Input and files
rules.text: All input (forms, API calls, headers, cookies, and data read from a database you do not control) MUST be validated on the server; SQL uses bound parameters, and output is escaped for where it lands. That guards against SQL injection and cross-site scripting (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Input and files
rules.text: Files from untrusted sources MUST be checked against the expected type, MUST NOT be passed to include, class-loading or reflection calls, MUST be stored outside the served folder with limited permissions, and MUST NOT be executable (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Banned patterns
rules.text: `env()` only in `config/` files, from Larastan's `NoEnvCallsOutsideOfConfig` rule. PROCTOR check: `env-outside-config` (a warning per call); the PHPStan rule is planned.

rules.heading: Banned patterns
rules.text: No disabled TLS verification, such as `withoutVerifying()` or `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER` set to false (OWASP ASVS). Planned.

rules.heading: Banned patterns
rules.text: No SQL built by joining strings; use bindings (OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet). Planned.

rules.heading: Banned patterns
rules.text: No debug leftovers or dynamic code, from `phpstan-disallowed-calls`. Planned.

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: ESLint flat config (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: `eslint-plugin-vue` `flat/recommended` (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: Prettier for formatting (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: `eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility` (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: Both JavaScript and TypeScript are linted (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: The stack's Vue starters use TypeScript; plain JavaScript stays fully supported (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: Node 22.13 or newer for the lint tools (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Security analysis
rules.text: The stack's GitLab instances run the Free tier, so nothing relies on GitLab SAST (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Security analysis
rules.text: The open tools instead: Larastan's env rule, `phpstan-disallowed-calls`, and a Psalm taint-analysis pilot on one app (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: How it is enforced
rules.text: Pint, PHPStan, Rector dry-runs and ESLint run in CI through Preflight components, not in the deploy gate (the stack's coding standard). The Preflight components are Planned.

rules.heading: How it is enforced
rules.text: New rules arrive as warnings and become errors on a stated date, the same staging as PHP versions (the stack's enforcement design).

rules.heading: How it is enforced
rules.text: PROCTOR reports whether an app uses the presets (the stack's coding standard). The PROCTOR report is Planned.

rules.heading: Not adopted
rules.text: Mago and PHP_CodeSniffer 4 are not adopted; Pint is the only formatter (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Not adopted
rules.text: Mago is looked at again before Pinstripe 1.0 (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: To be decided
rules.text: `declare(strict_types=1)` in every file. The sources recommend it, but the stack's coding standard does not decide it.

rules.heading: To be decided
rules.text: `phpstan-strict-rules` for the stack's packages (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: To be decided
rules.text: Where the ESLint package is published (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Names, comments and connections
rules.text: Table and column names are descriptive. Add table and column comments (Laravel's `->comment()`) where the database supports them, to say what an element is for (SHOULD) (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Names, comments and connections
rules.text: The connection between the app and the database MUST be encrypted. The database account MUST have only the privileges the app needs, never an administrator account (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Set `Schema::defaultStringLength(191)` in `AppServiceProvider::boot()`, before any migration runs. 5.6 caps an indexed `utf8mb4` column at 767 bytes, which is 191 characters. PROCTOR check: `mysql56`.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Keep `utf8mb4` and `utf8mb4_unicode_ci`, the defaults. Never use an 8.0-only collation such as `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci` (not yet confirmed on a 5.6 server).

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Store JSON as `text` or `longText`, with Eloquent `array` or `json` casts, and filter in PHP. 5.6 has no JSON column type. PROCTOR check: `mysql56`.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Leave `use_upsert_alias` unset, so `upsert()` uses `VALUES()`. The row alias that setting switches to needs MySQL 8.0.19.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Rename a column with raw `DB::statement('ALTER TABLE ... CHANGE ...')`. Avoid `renameColumn` and `renameIndex`, which emit 5.7 syntax. PROCTOR check: `mysql56`.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Use `Schema::hasTable` only. Column introspection is not reliable on 5.6 (not yet confirmed on a 5.6 server).

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Skip `db:show` and `db:monitor`, and run one database-queue worker (or another driver if the platform offers one). 5.6 has no `SKIP LOCKED`, so a single worker avoids double-processing.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Use `timestamp`, not `date`, for `useCurrent()`. A `date` column cannot take a current-timestamp default on 5.6.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Run migrations in CI against a real 5.6 container. SQLite-only tests pass code that 5.6 rejects.

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: No `dev-master`, `dev-*` or `*` constraints on runtime dependencies (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: `unbounded-constraints`.

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: A lock file is required and MUST be committed (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: `lock-committed`.

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: `composer audit` MUST report no advisories at or above the policy's severity threshold (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: `composer-audit`.

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: `composer.json` `require.php` MUST NOT allow an EOL version as its lowest bound (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: `php-floor`.

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: Apps SHOULD set a Composer cooldown of 3 days, once Composer 2.11 is stable and in the base images; until then no cooldown is set (the stack's dependency decision, 2026-11-03). A PROCTOR check for a missing cooldown is planned, not built.

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: Every project is a framework-free core plus thin adapters. `composer.json` requires only `php` and PSR packages; Laravel, Inertia and Vue are `suggest` (the stack's core-plus-adapters design).

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: Adapters call the core and never re-implement it (the stack's core-plus-adapters design).

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: Before adding a third-party package, check it comes from a trusted source, and where the source is open, read enough of it to judge it sound and fit (SHOULD). The audit and abandoned-package rules in this chapter apply after that choice (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Private packages
rules.text: Internal-only packages MUST be installed from one GitLab package registry per ecosystem (Composer, npm), not from one `vcs`, `path` or `artifact` repository entry per package (the stack's private-packages decision).

rules.heading: Private packages
rules.text: Credentials MUST NOT appear in any repository URL in `composer.json` or `composer.lock`, or as a literal value in a committed `.npmrc`. Tokens live in a gitignored `auth.json`, the npm user config, or a CI or build-time secret (the stack's private-packages decision). PROCTOR check: `repo-url-credentials`.

rules.heading: Private packages
rules.text: Builds MUST use a read-only deploy token (`read_package_registry` only); personal access tokens MUST NOT be used in builds (the stack's private-packages decision).

rules.heading: Private packages
rules.text: The private Composer registry entry MUST be canonical, and the Packagist entry SHOULD exclude the internal vendor names, so a public package with the same name can never be installed instead (the stack's private-packages decision).

rules.heading: Private packages
rules.text: A released version MUST map to one commit for ever: tags are protected, and a version is never republished from a different commit (the stack's private-packages decision).

rules.heading: Private packages
rules.text: Public code MUST NOT go through the private registry; it is published to Packagist or npm (the stack's private-packages decision).

rules.heading: Private packages
rules.text: Apps SHOULD NOT proxy or mirror public registries in v1 (the stack's private-packages decision).

rules.heading: Deploy gate
rules.text: The deploy-time rule set is small, offline and fast: the target image's status and its PHP version against `policy.json`, the framework and stack package versions in `composer.lock`, and known advisories from a cached database (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

rules.heading: Deploy gate
rules.text: EOL fails: a deploy that regresses a rule, a new app that fails any rule, or an expired override is blocked (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

rules.heading: Deploy gate
rules.text: It ratchets: a deploy that doesn't make things worse always passes (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

rules.heading: Deploy gate
rules.text: Each rule moves through stages, `report`, `warn`, `block`, with dates in `policy.json` (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

rules.heading: On Citadel
rules.text: Citadel runs the gate in its release hook: `proctor gate` in `runGitPull()`, against the fetched commit, before it is checked out (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

rules.heading: On Citadel
rules.text: The gate is pending the Citadel team, which is still an open question. Until it is adopted, enforcement is CI on the test GitLab instance (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

rules.heading: Elsewhere
rules.text: The same gate runs as a CI job through Preflight's `proctor` component, wherever the pipeline runs (first-repos).

rules.heading: Elsewhere
rules.text: Squire's `docker` target will run the gate before it ships an image, and so will its later `openshift` and `coolify` targets (the stack's rule that packages run on any container platform).

rules.heading: Every OS
rules.text: Every developer tool works on Windows, macOS and Linux (the stack's every-OS design).

rules.heading: Every OS
rules.text: A developer script ships as a `.ps1` and `.sh` pair that do the same thing, or as one PHP command, which works the same everywhere (the stack's every-OS design).

rules.heading: Every OS
rules.text: Windows gets PowerShell (`.ps1`), which never needs bash or WSL. Linux and macOS get bash (`.sh`), written for macOS's stock bash 3.2 and its BSD tools (the stack's every-OS design).

rules.heading: Every OS
rules.text: Every repo carries a `.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf`, and `.ps1`, `.bat` and `.cmd` set to CRLF. Anything that runs on a Linux host MUST be LF: on Citadel, and on OpenShift, Coolify or raw Docker elsewhere (the stack's every-OS design).

rules.heading: Every OS
rules.text: Paths are built with the language's path functions, and subprocesses start with argument arrays, never shell strings (the stack's every-OS design). PROCTOR check: `portability`.

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: Overrides are named, dated and visible (the stack's version policy).

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: An app keeps a `policy-overrides.json` with an expiry date and a reason (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: `overrides`.

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: Check prints every override on every run, and Fleet lists them (the stack's version policy).

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: An expired override is a failure (first-repos). PROCTOR check: `overrides`.

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: On the Citadel side, overrides are held by Citadel admins, per app and per rule, with an expiry, a reason and an approver. There is no permanent override (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

rules.heading: Environments
rules.text: Every environment more than one person can reach follows the whole handbook; only a developer's own machine is exempt (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Environments
rules.text: Keep at least a pre-production and a production environment, each with its own working copy of every piece, database and supporting services included (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Environments
rules.text: Each deployment SHOULD be isolated from the others (one container per app), so one compromise does not become many. This holds on Citadel, OpenShift, Coolify and plain Docker (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Environments
rules.text: Decide early whether the deployment is in disaster-recovery scope, and write the decision in the README (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Environments
rules.text: Back up anything kept outside source control, databases included. Say in the README how to restore one app (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Environments
rules.text: An app SHOULD be load tested in each environment where heavy use is expected (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Running safely
rules.text: The app and its scripts MUST run as a non-root, non-administrator user with the least access they need (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Running safely
rules.text: The web server MUST NOT list directory contents (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Running safely
rules.text: File permissions MUST be set per path; write access for the web server is granted only to specific files or folders, and mode `777` MUST NOT be used (WSU developer standards, 2024). PROCTOR check: `world-writable` (`chmod 777` in scripts, Dockerfiles, CI and PHP).

rules.heading: Running safely
rules.text: Debugging and diagnostic files, scripts, dumps and backups MUST NOT sit in the served folder (WSU developer standards, 2024). PROCTOR check: `served-folder` (`phpinfo()`, dumps, backups, logs, env files and `adminer*.php` under `public/`).

rules.heading: Running safely
rules.text: On failure the app degrades predictably and fails closed: an authentication error withholds access (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Running safely
rules.text: A person is told when something fails: a monitor calls `/up` on a schedule and alerts someone (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Running safely
rules.text: Logs are rotated or removed at a set interval; temporary files are cleaned up; uploaded files have a retention rule. Citadel rotates container logs; elsewhere the platform or the app MUST (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Running safely
rules.text: Where it is practical, an app SHOULD record an audit trail of changes to data and of successful and failed access to sensitive data (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Who can reach it
rules.text: Every app MUST set `robots.txt` to keep spiders out unless crawling is wanted (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Who can reach it
rules.text: Every app MUST limit access by network address to the audience it serves, as a second lock beside sign-in and never instead of it (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Who can reach it
rules.text: The one named exception: the stack's own public front pages are crawlable by design (the stack's agent-ready sites decision). It is a special case for those pages, not a general exemption for public pages.

rules.heading: Enforcement
rules.text: The runtime (Baseline) is enforcement point (a): it warns, and refuses only for unsafe config (the stack's enforcement design).

rules.heading: Headers
rules.text: Every response carries the same headers from HELMET (the stack's runtime and headers design): Content-Security-Policy: the WayneUI default policy plus a per-request nonce and `strict-dynamic`, with `frame-ancestors 'self'`, `base-uri 'self'`, `object-src 'none'` and `form-action 'self'` added. X-Content-Type-Options `nosniff`. X-Frame-Options `SAMEORIGIN`. Referrer-Policy `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`. Permissions-Policy, with camera, geolocation, microphone, payment and usb denied by default. Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy `same-origin`. Strict-Transport-Security `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`, on HTTPS responses only.

rules.heading: Headers
rules.text: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy is off by default (the stack's runtime and headers design).

rules.heading: Headers
rules.text: An app SHOULD NOT weaken the default Content-Security-Policy with `'unsafe-inline'` for scripts; it uses the nonce instead (the stack's runtime and headers design). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Proxy trust
rules.text: Behind a proxy the app sees the proxy's address, so `X-Forwarded-Proto` is honored only from a trusted proxy (the stack's runtime and headers design).

rules.heading: Proxy trust
rules.text: A platform preset (`citadel` or `docker`) names the trusted proxies; off the platform the app passes its own list. An unknown preset throws at boot (the stack's runtime and headers design).

rules.heading: Proxy trust
rules.text: No Strict-Transport-Security is sent for a request that was not really secure (the stack's runtime and headers design).

rules.heading: Sessions
rules.text: HELMET hardens the PHP session settings before the session starts (the stack's runtime and headers design).

rules.heading: Sessions
rules.text: The request-forgery guard (Sec-Fetch-Site, then Origin) is optional and off by default; a rejected request gets 403 `Forbidden` (the stack's runtime and headers design).

rules.heading: Health
rules.text: `/up` is the health endpoint HELMET answers for raw PHP apps (the stack's runtime and headers design).

rules.heading: Errors in production
rules.text: PHP `display_errors` MUST be `Off` and `log_errors` `On` in production (Squire's deploy kit ships that php.ini; HELMET neither sets nor checks it). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Errors in production
rules.text: Laravel `APP_DEBUG` MUST be `false` in production (WSU developer standards, 2024). The Laravel adapter writes one warning `helmet.debug_enabled_in_production` when it is true in the production environment.

rules.heading: Not decided here
rules.text: The Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy default.

rules.heading: Not decided here
rules.text: The Content-Security-Policy report endpoints.

rules.heading: Not decided here
rules.text: The metrics endpoint.

rules.heading: Credentials
rules.text: Credentials (database and service passwords, API keys, tokens) MUST NOT be committed to version control, because history keeps them forever. Commit `.env.example` with placeholders instead. A credential that was ever committed is treated as exposed and rotated (WSU developer standards, 2024). PROCTOR checks: `app-key` (a committed `.env` or `APP_KEY`) and `repo-url-credentials` (a token in a package source URL); no general secret scan exists yet.

rules.heading: Credentials
rules.text: Credentials and sensitive data MUST live outside any folder the web server serves. Laravel's `public/` is the only served folder; raw PHP apps serve one `public/` folder the same way (WSU developer standards, 2024). PROCTOR check: `served-folder` (dumps, backups, logs and env files in `public/`).

rules.heading: Credentials
rules.text: The Laravel `APP_KEY` is a credential: whoever holds it can forge encrypted payloads, which can mean code execution. It MUST NOT be committed, a key that leaked MUST be rotated with `php artisan key:generate` on every environment that used it, and the session driver SHOULD NOT be `cookie`, which seals every session with the key (GitGuardian, exploiting public APP_KEY leaks). PROCTOR check: `app-key`.

rules.heading: Credentials
rules.text: An app uses its own dedicated application ID, never a person's employee or student AccessID, to reach another server or service, with the fewest permissions the task needs (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Credentials
rules.text: Real values come from the environment at deploy time (the Citadel dashboard or CI variables), never from a file in the repo (WSU developer standards, 2024).

rules.heading: Errors and debug output
rules.text: `APP_DEBUG` MUST be `false` in production (WSU developer standards, 2024). The Laravel adapter writes one warning `helmet.debug_enabled_in_production` when it is true in the production environment. A PROCTOR check for this is proposed, not built.

rules.heading: Errors and debug output
rules.text: Public-facing code MUST NOT display default interpreter or framework error pages to the user; show a controlled message and log the detail (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Errors and debug output
rules.text: Logs and diagnostic output MUST NOT contain credentials or personally identifiable information such as Social Security numbers. That includes logged exceptions (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Not decided here
rules.text: The HELMET header rules and runtime refusals are written in `runtime-and-headers.md`.

rules.heading: Versions
rules.text: The dates live in `policy/policy.json`. Every tool derives a version's state from the date, through the CREED reader. No other code decides state (the stack's version policy).

rules.heading: Versions
rules.text: The PHP floor is `^8.2`, the oldest non-EOL version today (the stack's version policy). It moves to `^8.3` on 2027-01-01. PROCTOR check: `php-floor`.

rules.heading: Versions
rules.text: Stack packages raise their own `php` floor in a new major when a PHP version reaches EOL, so security fixes require the upgrade (the stack's version policy).

rules.heading: Versions
rules.text: `policy.json` is a contract, versioned like WayneUI's `/v2/`. Older Check versions MUST still read newer policy files (the stack's version policy).
